title: 45-year-old man with a cough
arrival: A 45-year-old man presents with a cough for five days.
feedbackWhy: This patient does not meet any red or yellow criteria. However, his SpO2 is below the high-risk threshold of 92%. He should not be moved directly to the low-acuity or waiting area without immediate review by a supervising clinician.
reviewNote: CLINICIAN REVIEW REQUIRED: confirm SpO2 90% is clinically consistent with RR 22 and no chest indrawing, and that no later value (HR 98, RR 22, Temp 37.8°C) risks a second high-risk vital sign. Every value is proposed.

design.intendedChallenge: A patient with no red or yellow finding can still have a high-risk vital sign. SpO2 is found only by measuring it, at the last step of the card.
design.expectedCommonError: triaging as green because nothing is found until the vital signs step.

airway_red.text: Speaks in full sentences. No stridor. No chest indrawing. No central cyanosis.

circulation_red.text: Pulse strong. Capillary refill 2 seconds. No bleeding.

disability_red.text: No convulsions. Alert with normal mental status. No headache. No stiff neck.

other_red.text: Age 45. No chest or abdominal pain. No trauma, poisoning, threatened limb or snake bite. Not aggressive.

airway_yellow.text: No swelling of the mouth, throat or neck. No wheezing.

circulation_yellow.text: No vomiting or diarrhoea. No bleeding or fainting. Not pale. Drinking normally.

disability_yellow.text: Alert and calm. Walking independently. No weakness. No visual disturbance. No pain.

other_yellow.text: No rash, deformity, fracture or dislocation. No trauma. No known surgical diagnosis. Passing urine normally. No bite or needlestick exposure.
